subject: EdgeNova — SDK local onramp checklist & auth/routing notes
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Qureshi <aisha@edgenova.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeNova — SDK local onramp checklist & auth/routing notes

Hi Aisha —

Great to meet you and the EdgeNova team on today's call. Quick recap + proposed local onramp checklist so your engineers can start experimenting with Redwood's SDKs while we scope the Dedicated deployment: 

1) Recap of call
- Primary use case: in-product assistant + semantic search over internal KB (200k docs).
- Latency target: 250ms p95 for chat flows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~30 req/sec, spikes to 120 req/sec during sync jobs.
- Must support embeddings + a lightweight reranker for search re-ranking.

2) Local quickstart (Python + TypeScript) — minimal steps (we'll provide repos):
- Python sandbox: python3.10, venv -> pip install redwood-inference
  * Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_BASE_URL env vars
  * Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx; export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwood.ai
- TypeScript sandbox: node 18+, yarn -> yarn add @redwood/inference
  * .env: REW_API_KEY and REW_BASE_URL (we'll include mapping file)

3) Auth & routing notes
- Recommend API keys for initial PoC. For production, we'll propose short-lived tokens via your IdP (Okta) and optional mTLS for Private deployments.
- If you plan to run behind a corporate proxy, please confirm outbound allowlist (we'll share IP ranges).

4) Structured output & tool calling
- Use our function-calling-compatible schema validator. We'll attach a short example that returns a strict JSON object to minimize post-processing.
- For tool-calling (external lookups) we'll show how to register a local webhook and enable signed callbacks.

5) Embeddings & rerankers
- We'll provide an embeddings quickstart that includes batching guidelines and an initial recommendation for vector size (1536) + quantized index options.
- For reranking, start with our lightweight reranker model (low-cost) and we can evaluate a higher-accuracy variant after baseline results.

6) Next steps / asks from EdgeNova
- Please share a short infra diagram (public Drive link or redacted) showing where requests originate and whether you'll host anything in a VPC.
- Confirm whether the PoC should hit our hosted API or a Private VPC deployment.
- Share an initial sample document set (small export ~500 docs) so we can validate embedding & reranker latency.

Attachments: edgenova-env-matrix.csv (template to capture your env details), redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (walking through local installs).

I'll follow up with sample repo links in a separate email. Happy to jump on a quick workshop next week if you'd like an engineer-led sandbox session.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0147

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our engineering lead: 

1) Auth: for the PoC we prefer API keys, but production will need Okta-based short-lived tokens. Can you share an example token exchange flow for Okta (refresh/token endpoints)?

2) Routing: we run most outbound through a corporate proxy (BlueGate). We'll need the IP ranges to allowlist. Can you confirm whether function/webhook callbacks support a static TLS cert?

3) Embeddings: our content has a lot of short snippets (product descriptions), will 1536 dims be overkill? Also, do you support incremental indexing (we append 2-3k docs/day)?

4) Reranker: do you have an opinionated starter prompt / pipeline we can try that runs client-side vs server-side? Latency is a concern.

We're uploading a redacted infra diagram to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeNovaOnramp (shared). I've attached a small token of our expected daily volume in edgenova-env-matrix.csv.

Can your team do a short 60-minute sandbox next Tue 21 May at 10:00 PT? Our engineers would like a live walkthrough of the Python quickstart.

Thanks,
Aisha Qureshi

Subject: Re: EdgeNova — SDK local onramp checklist & auth/routing notes

Aisha —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Answers inline below and a few extra setup commands to get you started locally.

1) Okta token exchange
- We recommend a short-lived JWT approach using your IdP. Basic flow:
  * EdgeNova IdP -> Redwood token exchange endpoint (mutual TLS optional) -> returns short-lived RBAC token for SDK calls.
  * We'll share a sample Node/Python token-exchange snippet in the quickstart repo (server side).

2) Allowlist & callbacks
- We'll send our hosted API IP ranges; for Private deployments callbacks can use your cert (mutual TLS supported).

3) Embeddings dims & incremental indexing
- 1536 is a good default for balanced recall. For mostly short snippets you can try 768 to save vector index memory — we'll include both options and benchmark.
- Incremental indexing supported; our batching recommendations are in the attachment (edgenova-env-matrix.csv).

4) Reranker pipeline
- Starter pipeline: client sends top-K via semantic search -> server reranker model scores top-K -> final results returned. For low-latency, run the reranker in a Dedicated node group with batching disabled and use the lightweight variant. We'll include a sample prompt & temperature.

Local install snippets:
- Python:
  python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  pip install --upgrade pip
  pip install redwood-inference

  # quick test (replace env var first)
  python -c "from redwood import Client; c=Client(); print(c.health())"

- TypeScript:
  mkdir ts-quickstart && cd ts-quickstart
  yarn init -y && yarn add @redwood/inference
  # quick test
  node -e "const { Client } = require('@redwood/inference'); const c=new Client(); c.health().then(console.log).catch(console.error)"

Structured output & function-calling example (Python)
- We'll include a short snippet in the attached redwood-sdk-quickstart.md that demonstrates:
  * defining a JSON schema for expected output
  * using the SDK's function_call wrapper to enforce the schema

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (contains token-exchange code, example prompts, and quickstart repo links).

Regarding the sandbox on Tue 21 May 10:00 PT — that works for our engineer (Hannah). Can you confirm attendees so we can send a calendar invite?

Best,
Logan
